My dear [Ellie](/person/663)
I am delighted to hear of the Medallion![^1]
Have you seen Sir Herbert Maxwell’s book of the months-? He disbelieved the rod and someone ought to write to him. He watched [Mullins](/person/2189) - and fancied he had discovered the places before. But [Lady Crawley](/person/2188), the mother of [Mrs William Gibbs](/person/557), who had the power only in that generation of the family laughed at it as imagination, and I believe Mrs Gibbs inherited it, but never spoke of it. [Mrs Monroe](/person/1033) had Mullins to find water at Colden Common and he did. All the servants tried under his tuition but only one maid succeeded.
I am doing our Birds with anecdotes if possible to add to the book.
[Helen](/person/1613) has a copy of [illegible] marked by her [father](/person/1624) and can complete the set. There really is much to say of them.
Your affectionate

C M Yonge


[^1]: A medallion is mentioned in [John Keble\'s Parishes](/book/247), 3, which is the book under discussion here.
